questions.question: If your trailer goes off course while backing, what should you do?

options.text: Continue backing without making any changes.
Pull forward, adjust your position, and back again.
Get out and move the trailer by hand.
Turn the steering wheel all the way left until the trailer straightens.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull forward, adjust your position, and back again.
questions.explanation: If your trailer goes off course while backing, pull forward and reposition your vehicle. Then continue backing.

questions.question: How do loaded rigs compare to empty rigs in terms of rollover risk?

options.text: They are less likely to roll over.
They are more likely to roll over.
They have the same rollover risk.
They should not be driven.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are more likely to roll over.
questions.explanation: Loaded rigs have a higher center of gravity because of the cargo weight. This makes them 10 times more likely to roll over in a crash than empty rigs.

questions.question: Trailers built after which year must have Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS)?
questions.explanation: Trailers and converter dollies made on or after March 1, 1998 must have Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS).

questions.question: When connecting air brake hoses, what should you do?

options.text: Connect the correct matching glad hands.
Connect only one set of glad hands.
Leave one glad hand loose.

questions.correctAnswerText: Connect the correct matching glad hands.
questions.explanation: Connect matching glad hands to each other. They are often color-coded to help you avoid mistakes. Blue is usually for service lines and red is usually for emergency lines.

questions.question: When testing ____, move forward slowly and apply the hand brake control.

options.text: The Anti-Lock Braking System
The emergency braking system
The trailer service brakes

questions.explanation: To test the trailer service brakes, make sure the air pressure is normal and release the parking brake. Move forward slowly and use the hand control to apply the brakes. You should feel the trailer brakes activate if they work properly.

questions.question: How can you avoid needing to make sudden lane changes?

options.text: Use your horn to make other drivers move.
Drive slower than the speed limit.
Watch the road ahead while driving.
Pull off the road when traffic is heavy.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch the road ahead while driving.
questions.explanation: Sudden lane changes are dangerous with large vehicles. Look ahead for obstacles so you can plan lane changes in advance instead of making sudden ones.

questions.question: When connecting a trailer, what should you do with the glad hands?

options.text: Connect the correct matching glad hands.
Glad hands can connect to any other glad hands.
Connect only one set of glad hands.

questions.correctAnswerText: Connect the correct matching glad hands.
questions.explanation: Connect matching glad hands to each other. They are often color-coded to help you avoid mistakes. Blue is usually for service lines and red is usually for emergency lines.

questions.question: What can happen if the fifth wheel plate is not properly greased?

options.text: The trailer can disconnect.
Steering problems can occur.
Braking problems can occur.
The lights can be affected.

questions.explanation: If the fifth wheel plate is not properly lubricated, friction between the tractor and trailer increases. This causes steering problems.

questions.question: What is true about combination vehicles compared to single commercial vehicles?

options.text: They are usually shorter.
They are usually lighter.
They require more driving skill.
They are easier to drive.

questions.explanation: Combination vehicles are heavier and longer than single commercial vehicles. Because of this, they require more driving skill.

questions.question: If your trailer drifts while backing, which way should you turn the steering wheel?

options.text: Return it to the 12 o'clock position.
Turn it toward the direction of the drift.
Turn it away from the direction of the drift.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn it toward the direction of the drift.
questions.explanation: If your trailer drifts while backing, immediately correct it by turning the top of the steering wheel toward the direction of the drift.

questions.question: How can a driver prevent a rollover?

options.text: Keep cargo low.
Place cargo high.
Keep cargo loose.
Turn quickly.

questions.explanation: Rollovers can happen when you turn too quickly. Keep the vehicle's center of gravity low by loading cargo as close to the ground as possible.

questions.question: What is one benefit of keeping cargo low?

options.text: Prevent a rollover.
Help you drive faster.
Make turns more dangerous.

questions.explanation: Keeping cargo low lowers the vehicle's center of gravity. This helps prevent rollovers when you turn.

questions.question: Are trailers built before 1975 required to have spring brakes?

options.text: Yes, they must have spring brakes.
No, they are not required to have spring brakes.
They are unsafe to drive.
They cannot be driven on public roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, they are not required to have spring brakes.
questions.explanation: Trailers built before 1975 do not need spring brakes. When parking these trailers, use wheel chocks to prevent them from rolling.

questions.question: If you are unsure about your path while backing, what should you do?

options.text: Continue backing.
Stop and get out to look.
Continue backing, but go slower.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and get out to look.
questions.explanation: Stop the vehicle, get out, and check your path before backing up again.

questions.question: What should you do before starting a trip?

options.text: Leave the service line valve open.
Remove the relay valves.
Close the emergency line valve.

questions.explanation: Before driving, open both the rear emergency line and service line valves to check for air. Listen for air escaping. Then close both valves before you start driving.

questions.question: How should cargo be loaded to prevent a rollover?

options.text: Load most weight on the driver's side.
Place most weight near the rear.
Spread weight evenly throughout the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Spread weight evenly throughout the trailer.
questions.explanation: Distribute cargo weight evenly in the trailer. Do not put too much weight on one side.

questions.question: When backing a trailer, which way should you first turn the steering wheel?

options.text: In the direction you want the trailer to go.
In the opposite direction of where you want the trailer to go.
To the left.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the opposite direction of where you want the trailer to go.
questions.explanation: When backing with a trailer, turn the wheel the opposite way first. Once the trailer starts to turn, turn the wheel the other way to follow it.

questions.question: If your vehicle gets stuck on railroad tracks, what should you do?

options.text: Stay in the cab and call for help.
Exit the vehicle and walk away from the tracks.
Signal another driver to push your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Exit the vehicle and walk away from the tracks.
questions.explanation: Leave the vehicle immediately and walk away from the tracks. Call emergency services.

questions.question: Driving a combination vehicle requires ____ driving a single vehicle.

options.text: Less skill than
About the same level of skill as
More skill than
Exactly the same level of skill as

questions.explanation: Combination vehicles need more skill to drive. They are longer, heavier, and more likely to roll over.

questions.question: How many air lines does a combination vehicle have?

options.text: One
Two
Three
Four

questions.explanation: Every combination vehicle has two air lines: the service line and the emergency line.
